1.name: The Porters' Stroll
1.desc: The market's loading crew all went for a walk in the square today, to "have a proper talk about life".
lines: After the walk, the whole crew drops by your place for a rest.

2.name: Afternoon Nap
2.desc: Napping after lunch is all the rage in the neighborhood. All afternoon the street is as quiet as a holiday.
lines: The customers who just woke up are in a lovely mood, though.

3.name: Before You Enter
3.desc: New town rule: before coming in, customers must read a "Dining Preferences Notice" and tick "I agree" item by item. How will you lay it out?
lines: Make a big "Accept all" button
Customers get in fast, then find they've been recommended a pile of dishes they don't want.
List every item honestly
A queue forms at the door, but the inspector praises your compliance.

4.name: The Clock Jumped Ahead
4.desc: Last night the clock tower moved itself forward an hour. Half the town is on the new time, half on the old.
lines: The lunch crowd arrives in two waves.

5.name: The Song Contest Next Door
5.desc: Tonight the TV is showing the next town's song contest. Each costume is wilder than the last, and nobody can explain the scoring. Who are you rooting for?
lines: The twins in tinfoil capes
They won! You cheer at the top of your lungs, and your customers pop the champagne.
They didn't win. You hummed along all night and lost your voice, but you're in a good mood.
The grandpa who sings every song on one note
Grandpa won! You cheer at the top of your lungs, and your customers pop the champagne.
Grandpa didn't win. You hummed along all night and lost your voice, but you're in a good mood.
The electro band with the smoke machine
The band won! You cheer at the top of your lungs, and your customers pop the champagne.
The band didn't win. You hummed along all night and lost your voice, but you're in a good mood.

6.name: Form 27-B
6.desc: A letter from the town hall: the font on your sign isn't in the "Approved Fonts Catalog". Please fill in Form 27-B, attach three supporting documents and get two stamps.
lines: Do it properly
A whole morning of running around. Very educational.
Use the form to prop up a table leg
The table no longer wobbles, but an inspector passing by in the afternoon gives you a long look.

7.name: A Crate of Empties
7.desc: There's a crate of empty bottles in the back alley. The old lady next door says you get a deposit back on every one.
lines: Return them
You get a small handful of coins back.
Give them to the old man who checks the bins every day
He sings your praises to everyone he meets.

8.name: The New Roundabout
8.desc: A new roundabout just opened at the edge of town. Riders go in and can't find the way out, looping round and round.
lines: Deliveries are slower, but all that spinning counts as exercise.

9.name: The Selfie-Stick Tour
9.desc: A tour group waving long sticks squeezes into your restaurant. Every dish gets five minutes of photos before anyone takes a bite.
lines: It's lively in here, but the customers have gotten pickier.

10.name: A Note on the Door
10.desc: The place across the street has a note taped to its door: "Gone to the seaside. See you next month."
lines: Its regulars have no choice but to come to you.

11.name: Quiet Notice
11.desc: A notice goes up around town: no loud chopping at Sunday lunchtime.
lines: The kitchen works on tiptoe, and slow and careful turns out finer food.

12.name: Fruit in Savory Dishes?
12.desc: Two tables are arguing over whether sweet fruit belongs in a savory dish, and they insist you settle it.
lines: It does
The adventurous eaters stay.
It doesn't
The traditionalists are so pleased they order an extra dish.
Hide in the kitchen
While hiding, you find a voucher under a cupboard.

13.name: The Inspector in a Bow Tie
13.desc: An inspector in a bow tie points at your menu: that sauce may only bear its name if it's made in a certain valley.
lines: Rename it "Something-Style Sauce"
The name got longer, and customers hesitate when ordering.
Invite him to taste a bowl on the spot
He's silent for a long time after eating: "Hmm... perhaps that valley could be a little bigger."

14.name: The Square's Pigeons
14.desc: A flock of pigeons from the square is squabbling over breadcrumbs right outside your door.
lines: Customers give it a wide berth.

15.name: A Perfectly Straight Queue
15.desc: Somehow, a long, perfectly straight queue has formed outside your door all by itself.
lines: Everyone is very polite. Nobody cuts in, and nobody dares ask what they're actually queuing for.

16.name: The Pot at the Flea Market
16.desc: At the weekend flea market there's a blackened old pot. The seller says it was his great-grandfather's and lets it go cheap.
lines: Buy it
Just an ordinary old pot, but food cooked in it tastes richer.
There's a line of tiny writing on the bottom. You pry it open and find two vouchers tucked inside.
Leave it
You run a hand over the handle, then put it back.

17.name: The Runaway Pig
17.desc: The neighbor's runaway pig spent all morning rooting around your backyard, and dug up a black, very pungent lump.
lines: Return the pig, and the lump, to the neighbor
The neighbor thanks you with a basket of ingredients.
Keep it and experiment
You shave a tiny bit into a dish, and customers keep asking for the recipe.

18.name: Round the Maypole
18.desc: The town's young people danced all night around a pole covered in flowers.
lines: At dawn they all come running for hot soup.

19.name: Match Night
19.desc: Tonight two towns' teams face off, and everyone is crammed into any place with a TV.
lines: Bring in a TV
Full house, and very loud.
No TV: keep a quiet spot for those who want one
Everyone who comes just wants a peaceful meal.

20.name: Balcony Choir
20.desc: Every evening, the people in the building opposite sing together on their balconies, and the whole street leans out to listen.
lines: When the song ends, they pop downstairs for dinner.

21.name: Car-Free Day
21.desc: The town is holding a "Car-Free Day". There's nothing on the main street but bikes.
lines: Your riders have a clear run all day.

22.name: Sauna, Then Snow
22.desc: The bathhouse owner invites you to join everyone for a sauna, then a roll in the snow.
lines: Go
You come back glowing and chop faster than ever.
Hand out towels from the side
Everyone remembers you.

23.name: The 64-Piece Table
23.desc: Your new table comes in 64 pieces, with instructions that are all pictures and no words.
lines: Once it's built there are three screws left over. It wobbles a little, but customers find it charming.

24.name: The Bus Go-Slow
24.desc: Today the bus drivers are sticking strictly to the minimum legal speed, and the whole town is late for work.
lines: On the bright side, the roads are empty.

25.name: Long Weekend
25.desc: Monday is a holiday, and family after family has wheeled their suitcases out of town.
lines: The ones who stayed are your big-spending regulars.

26.name: The Chalet Market
26.desc: A row of little wooden huts has popped up in the square, and the air smells of mulled wine and roasted chestnuts.
lines: Everyone worn out from browsing squeezes into your place.

27.name: A Truckload of Tomatoes
27.desc: The next town's tomato-throwing festival is over, and there's a whole truckload of tomatoes left, going cheap.
lines: Buy the lot
The whole truckload is yours.
Pass
As the truck pulls away, one tomato tumbles off and lands right at your feet.

28.name: Storks on the Chimney
28.desc: A pair of white storks has built a nest on your chimney.
lines: The old folks on the corner say it means good luck is on its way.

29.name: Sale Season
29.desc: The whole town has gone into sale season. Even the Market stalls have hung up "15% off everything".
lines: More people are out shopping.

30.name: Dinner at Ten
30.desc: A big group turns up for dinner at ten at night.
lines: They talk and eat into the small hours.

31.name: A Quick One at the Counter
31.desc: The new customers just stand at the counter, knock back one small glass and go.
lines: They come and go so fast the kitchen can't keep up.

32.name: Harvest Crew
32.desc: The vineyard up the hill has hired a big crew to pick grapes.
lines: When they knock off at noon, they all come to you for lunch.

33.name: Four O'Clock
33.desc: At four sharp, the whole street drops what it's doing for tea and a couple of biscuits.
lines: Tea drinkers pop in on their way.

34.name: Kettles On
34.desc: The moment the evening soap ends, the whole town gets up to boil the kettle, and the power trips with a "click".
lines: You have to relight the stoves, but in that minute of darkness, the customers chat even more.

35.name: The Runaway Cheese
35.desc: Someone rolled a whole wheel of cheese down the hill, and the whole town is chasing after it.
lines: Join the chase
You took a tumble, but everyone had a good laugh.
You caught the cheese first!
Sell hot soup at the bottom of the hill
The worn-out chasers all come for soup.

36.name: Weather Talk
36.desc: Every customer today chats with you about the weather for ten minutes on the way in.
lines: It's slow, but after a good chat nobody's picky.

37.name: Sorry, Sorry
37.desc: A customer stepped on your foot. You both said "sorry" at the same time, then apologized to each other five more times.
lines: The whole restaurant has become extremely polite.

38.name: The Double-Decker
38.desc: A new red double-decker bus route has opened.
lines: Tourists on the top deck get a perfect view of your sign.

39.name: Bonfire and Fireworks Night
39.desc: On this autumn evening, the town lights a huge bonfire and sets off fireworks. Someone even tossed a scarecrow onto the fire.
lines: Everyone's hungry after the fireworks.

40.name: Quiz Night at the Bar
40.desc: The bar is holding a quiz tonight. Three questions: get them all right and you take home the jar of vouchers on the counter.
lines: Not a single one right. At least you got a free ginger beer.
One right. The bartender gives you a voucher.
Two right. The bartender gives you a voucher.
All correct! The jar of vouchers on the counter is yours.

41.name: Beans on Toast
41.desc: A customer orders "beans, on top of toast". The head chef falls silent.
lines: Make it
The customer is moved almost to tears.
Talk him into something else
He reluctantly orders your house specialty.

42.name: The Driver Who Knew Every Street
42.desc: A taxi driver spent three years learning the name of every lane and alley in town.
lines: When he comes in to eat, he mentions a shortcut to your riders.

43.name: No Umbrellas Left
43.desc: Every umbrella in the stand by the door has been borrowed. Customers come in soaking wet.
lines: They ask for hot soup the moment they sit down.

44.name: The Long Neck in the Lake
44.desc: Someone claims to have seen a huge long-necked monster in the lake outside town, but every photo comes out blurry. Tourists flood in.
lines: Go take a look at the lake too
You got a photo! A bit blurry, though.
You got a photo of a floating log.
Stay and look after the tourists
Tourists fill every seat in your restaurant.

45.name: Strawberries and Cream
45.desc: The town tennis tournament has begun, and every spectator has a bowl of strawberries and cream.
lines: Desserts are flying off the counter.

46.name: The Five-Day Match
46.desc: The town's big match has been going for five days with no winner yet. They even stopped for afternoon tea.
lines: The fans come in to eat on the dot every day.

47.name: Bagpipes at the Door
47.desc: A man in a tartan kilt has started playing the bagpipes outside your door, and half the dogs on the street are howling along.
lines: Give him a few coins to play outside someone else's door
Peace returns to your doorstep.
Invite him in to eat
After his meal he plays a very slow tune, and the whole restaurant falls silent.

48.name: Paper Crowns
48.desc: Your customers pull open colorful party crackers with a bang.
lines: Everyone puts on a paper crown, and they take turns reading out the terrible jokes inside.

49.name: The Ginger Cat's Table
49.desc: A ginger cat has claimed a table for a nap, and nothing will wake it.
lines: Customers line up to pet it.

50.name: The Coin on Its Edge
50.desc: A coin fell off the counter and landed standing on its edge.
lines: You have a feeling today's your lucky day.

51.name: The Heartbroken Head Chef
51.desc: The head chef just got dumped, and every dish is a little too salty today.
lines: But everyone who eats them says: "There's a story in this food."

52.name: The Recipe on the Napkin
52.desc: In the middle of the night you dreamed up a brilliant new dish and got up to write it on a napkin. In the morning, it's just a line of scribbles.
lines: Still, you feel inspired all day.

53.name: Roach Meeting
53.desc: The roaches in the corner seem to be holding a meeting, lined up in a neat row.
lines: All in a row, they're easy to squash.

54.name: The Wrong Delivery
54.desc: A takeaway order from another restaurant was dropped at your door by mistake. It smells delicious.
lines: Take it back to that restaurant
Its owner treats you to a pastry.
Open it and study the recipe
You learn a thing or two, but feel a bit guilty.

55.name: The Freezer Blackout
55.desc: The kitchen freezer lost power for an hour last night. Nothing spoiled, but you broke out in a cold sweat.
lines: You're extra careful today.

56.name: Riverside Movie Night
56.desc: Someone has strung up a big white sheet by the river for an open-air movie.
lines: When it's over, nobody wants to go home.

57.name: Marathon Day
57.desc: The town is holding a marathon, and the main road is closed all morning.
lines: Your riders have to take the back streets.

58.name: Masked Diners
58.desc: It's the town's masked festival, and every customer comes in wearing a mask.
lines: You can't tell who your regulars are, but they're having a wonderful time.

59.name: White Asparagus
59.desc: The Market is piled high with white asparagus.
lines: Every customer's first words through the door: "Got any asparagus?"

60.name: The Sun That Won't Set
60.desc: It's eleven at night, and the sun is still hanging in the sky.
lines: Customers finish eating and still won't leave.

61.name: The Day That Never Dawned
61.desc: It's barely gotten light all day.
lines: Everyone lights candles, wraps up in blankets and takes their time over a meal.

62.name: Eggs in the Grass
62.desc: A bunch of kids are hunting for painted eggs in the grass in your backyard. They ask if you'd like to join in.
lines: Join the hunt
You found 1 egg.
You found 2 eggs.
You found 3 eggs.
Make snacks for the kids instead
The parents all turn up too.

63.name: Clinking Glasses
63.desc: Table after table of customers in leather shorts are clinking glasses along the long tables.
lines: They sing songs nobody else can understand.

64.name: This Year's New Wine
64.desc: This year's new wine went on sale today. Every shop on the street has hung a little sign by the door.
lines: You hang one up too.

65.name: Tractors Come to Town
65.desc: A convoy of tractors has rolled into town and jammed the roads solid. The farmers say they've come to "make their point", trailers piled with potatoes.
lines: Bring them some water
Before they leave, the farmers press a sack of potatoes on you.
Shut the door and lie low
You shut the door and lie low for a while.

66.name: One Cable for All
66.desc: New town rule: every charger must use the same kind of plug.
lines: Customers no longer have to go round borrowing charging cables.

67.name: The Cucumber Inspector
67.desc: An inspector has come with a protractor to measure your cucumbers. Ones that curve too much can't be called "Class I Cucumbers".
lines: Cooperate fully
He measures all afternoon, then presents you with a certificate.
Offer him a cucumber salad
When he's finished he says: "The curvy ones are nice too."

68.name: The Two-Hour Lunch
68.desc: Today's customers take two hours over lunch.
lines: Starter, main, dessert, coffee: not one can be skipped.

69.name: Thanks in Five Languages
69.desc: A table orders in five different languages. Between pointing and guessing, you somehow get every dish right.
lines: By the time they leave, you know five ways to say "thank you".

70.name: Monastery Honey
70.desc: Monks from the monastery up the hill have come down to sell their own honey, made, they say, to a recipe centuries old.
lines: Buy a jar
It goes into your desserts.
Pass
The monk gives you a piece of beeswax anyway: "May your pots never burn."

71.name: Last Orders
71.desc: The bell rings behind the bar and someone shouts: "Last orders!"
lines: Everyone rushes to order one last bite.

72.name: Fish on Friday
72.desc: Every Friday, the whole street smells of fried fish and vinegar.
lines: Table after table follows their noses to your door.

73.name: Sunday Roast
73.desc: At Sunday lunchtime, families come in for a roast, served with little batter puddings that puff up in the oven.
lines: Every family orders enough to cover a big table.

74.name: Three Cups, One Teabag
74.desc: You catch the head chef making three cups of tea from one teabag. He calls it "sensible living".
lines: Soon the whole kitchen is saving too.

75.name: The Gnome by the Door
75.desc: At some point a little clay gnome in a red hat appeared by the door, and every morning he's in a new pose.
lines: Nobody admits to putting him there.

76.name: Picnic in the Rain
76.desc: A family insisted on having their picnic in the rain, and ate their sandwiches under umbrellas.
lines: Then they ran into your place for hot soup.

77.name: Four on the Crossing
77.desc: Tourists are queuing at the zebra crossing outside your door, walking across in groups of four for photos, copying a certain old album cover.
lines: Photos done, they drop in for a sit-down.

78.name: Sheep on the Road
78.desc: A huge flock of sheep is blocking the road into town. The shepherd is in no hurry, so the riders have to go the long way round.
lines: Help drive the sheep
He gives you a piece of his homemade cheese.
Wait for them to pass
The flock finally ambles by, and deliveries are running way behind.

79.name: The Trolley and the Wall
79.desc: A tourist keeps pushing a luggage trolley into your wall, over and over, saying he's looking for a "platform".
lines: In the end he sits down for a meal.

80.name: New Year's Day Dip
80.desc: On the first morning of the year, a crowd in swimsuits charges into the icy sea.
lines: Back on dry land, they all charge into your place for hot soup.

81.name: The Rubber Duck Race
81.desc: Hundreds of rubber ducks are about to race down the river. A duck costs a few coins, and the money goes to the town's primary school.
lines: Buy a duck
Your duck bobs over the finish line first!
Your duck got stuck in the reeds. Still, the money went to a good cause, and that feels nice.
Watch from the bank
You cheer on every single duck from the bank.

82.name: Rehearsal
82.desc: The town's theater troupe has borrowed your restaurant to rehearse a play that's several centuries old.
lines: By the end of the afternoon, you know every line by heart.

83.name: Mint Sauce
83.desc: A customer orders roast lamb and insists on a bowl of green mint sauce with it.
lines: Whip some up right away
He finishes every bite, perfectly content.
Suggest he try your own sauce
He takes a taste and nods.

84.name: A Polite Complaint
84.desc: A customer finishes and says, very politely: "Not bad."
lines: You spend the whole afternoon wondering whether that was praise or an insult.

85.name: The Singing Dishwasher
85.desc: Today the dishwasher's noises sound a lot like a song.
lines: Everyone in the kitchen hums along.

86.name: The Forgotten Umbrella
86.desc: A customer left their umbrella here yesterday.
lines: Today they came back for it and insisted you take a voucher as thanks.

87.name: A Successful Proposal
87.desc: A customer got down on one knee in your restaurant and proposed. It's a yes!
lines: The whole room applauds, and several tables order more.

88.name: A Proposal Gone Wrong
88.desc: A customer proposes in your restaurant, and the answer is "Let me think about it." Things are a little awkward.
lines: Send over a dessert
He thanks you, eyes red.
Quickly put on something upbeat
The whole room breathes a sigh of relief.

89.name: A Child's Drawing
89.desc: A little kid drew your restaurant, and drew you as a big round head.
lines: You stick the drawing up on the wall.

90.name: Salt for Sugar
90.desc: The apprentice mixed up the salt jar and the sugar jar.
lines: Every dish all morning tastes a bit off, but you live and learn.

91.name: The Broken Spatula
91.desc: The spatula you've used for five years snapped today.
lines: You stand over it in silence for a moment, then go and find a new one.

92.name: The New Apprentice
92.desc: The new apprentice cuts potatoes into chunks of every size.
lines: Customers find it odd, but the apprentice is learning fast.

93.name: Renovations Next Door
93.desc: The place next door has started renovating.
lines: The drilling goes on from morning till night.

94.name: The New Neighbors
94.desc: The renovations next door are finally finished.
lines: The new neighbors bring over a plate of pastries to apologize for the noise.

95.name: The Food Blogger
95.desc: A food blogger spends the whole afternoon filming in your restaurant, phone held high.
lines: Every dish has to be shot from three angles.

96.name: "The Soup Was Too Hot"
96.desc: A bad review appeared online: "The soup was too hot."
lines: Reply politely and promise a warning next time
Someone liked your reply.
Ignore it
A few customers read the review and didn't come in.

97.name: Seven Sneezes
97.desc: The head chef sneezes seven times in a row.
lines: The neighbors say it means someone is thinking of him.

98.name: The Crow's Gift
98.desc: The crow that perches on your sign every day brought a shiny bottle cap today.
lines: It leaves the cap on your windowsill.

99.name: The One-Station Radio
99.desc: The kitchen radio only picks up one station.
lines: The same song loops from morning till noon.

100.name: The Customer Without a Wallet
100.desc: A customer finishes eating, pats his pockets, and says he forgot his money.
lines: Let him pay next time
Three days later he came back, with a thank-you gift on top.
You never saw him again.
Have him wash dishes to pay it off
He gets them sparkling.

101.name: Napkin Boats
101.desc: A child folded every napkin on the table into a little boat.
lines: The customers can't bring themselves to unfold them.

102.name: The Lost Rider
102.desc: A rider got lost and kept going all the way to the next town.
lines: He came back with a bag of their local specialties.

103.name: The Stopped Clock
lines: Nobody knows what time it is, and somehow nobody's in a rush.

104.name: Tea After Closing
104.desc: After closing, you sit alone in the empty restaurant with a cup of tea.
lines: You think this is a pretty good little place.

105.name: The Crooked Sign
105.desc: A gust of wind knocked your sign askew.
lines: Passers-by think it's a new restaurant and come in for a look.

106.name: The Traveler in the Fog
106.desc: A traveler lost in the fog feels his way into your restaurant.
lines: He says he followed the smell.

107.name: The End of the Rainbow
107.desc: They say there's a pot of gold buried at the end of the rainbow, and it ends right in your backyard.
lines: Dig
You dig up a rusty pot, and there really is something inside!
You dig up an old boot.
Don't dig
You decide to let the legend stay a legend.

108.name: The Snowman in a Chef's Hat
108.desc: Someone built a snowman outside your door, and it's wearing your chef's hat.
lines: Every customer wants a photo with it.

109.name: A Low Hum
109.desc: A bolt of lightning hit the town's lightning rod.
lines: Your wok gave a low "hummm", and ever since, everything you cook in it tastes amazing.

110.name: The Stargazers
110.desc: A group of stargazers turns up lugging telescopes.
lines: They sit in your restaurant all night, ordering pot after pot of hot tea.

111.name: The Solo Diner
111.desc: A customer in sunglasses sits alone in the corner, takes one bite of each dish, then jots something in a little notebook.
lines: Treat him specially: two extra dishes on the house
He nods, closes the notebook and leaves.
Treat him like everyone else
He finishes, closes the notebook and leaves.

112.name: A Review in the Paper
112.desc: The Town Daily ran an anonymous food review, and it's about your restaurant.
lines: "Service attentive to the point of suspicion, but the food is genuinely good."

113.name: A Little Plaque
113.desc: Someone mailed you a small brass plaque engraved with a single star. No name.
lines: You hang it by the door.

114.name: The Violin on the Corner
114.desc: A young man is playing the violin on the street corner, with only two coins in his case.
lines: Drop in a few coins
He gives you a nod.
Invite him in for a bowl of noodles
He eats with gusto and says he'll repay you one day.

115.name: The Show in the Square
115.desc: The young violinist is putting on a show in the square.
lines: After one song, he says: "This one's for the restaurant on the corner."

116.name: The Album Cover
lines: The cover is a picture of your front door.

117.name: The Expedition Arrives
117.desc: A scientific expedition has come to study the lake.
lines: They book your restaurant for lunch and dinner.

118.name: A Shadow on the Sonar
118.desc: A long shadow has shown up on the expedition's sonar. The team leader asks you: do you believe there's something in the lake?
lines: I believe
The leader gives you a sonar printout as a keepsake.
I don't
The leader laughs: "Neither do I, but that's what they pay me for."

119.name: The Expedition Report
119.desc: The expedition report is out. Conclusion: "A log with a lot of personality."
lines: Somehow, even more tourists turn up.

120.name: The Parrot Drops In
120.desc: The neighbor's parrot flew into your kitchen and spent the afternoon there.
lines: It learned to shout the name of your house specialty.

121.name: The Street Crier
121.desc: That parrot has taken up a perch at the end of the street.
lines: It shouts your house specialty over and over.

122.name: The Parrot's New Phrase
122.desc: The parrot has learned a new phrase: "Too expensive!" It's been shouting it outside your door all morning.
lines: Teach it to say "Delicious!"
After a whole afternoon, it finally gets it.
Make peace with a handful of sunflower seeds
It stops shouting and starts singing instead.

123.name: Two Candidates
123.desc: The merchants' association is electing a new president. The baker and the mechanic both drop by your place to canvass for votes.
lines: Back the baker
You stick a little note on your door backing the baker.
Back the mechanic
You stick a little note on your door backing the mechanic.

124.name: Debate Night
124.desc: The two candidates hold their debate in your restaurant.
lines: Curious onlookers pack the place.

125.name: Election Results
lines: Watch the count in the square
Your candidate won! On their very first day, the new president comes to eat at your place.
Your candidate lost. The new president still comes in for a bowl, and hopes you'll back them next time.
Wait for the news at the restaurant
Your candidate won! On their very first day, the new president comes to eat at your place.
Your candidate lost. The new president still comes in for a bowl, and hopes you'll back them next time.

126.name: Film Crew
126.desc: A film crew borrowed your restaurant to shoot a scene.
lines: Once word got out, the whole town came to watch.

127.name: The Bottle in the Cellar
127.desc: In a corner of the cellar you find a dusty old bottle of wine. The year on the label is older than you are.
lines: Sell it to the town's collector
The collector snaps it up on the spot and gives you a stack of vouchers for it.
Keep it on display behind the bar
The longer you look at that old bottle on the bar, the luckier today feels.

128.name: Meteor Shower
128.desc: There's a meteor shower tonight. You make a wish on the first shooting star.
lines: Early next morning, there are three vouchers in your mailbox.

129.name: The Handwritten Recipe Book
129.desc: After her meal, an old lady leaves behind a handwritten recipe book.
lines: She walked out without a word.

130.name: The Lottery Winner
130.desc: A customer scratches a winning lottery ticket right there at the table.
lines: He shouts: "Everyone's meal is on me today!"

131.name: Town-Wide Blackout
131.desc: The power is out all over town.
lines: Only your stoves are still burning, and people come by candlelight to eat.

132.name: Hail Through the Awning
132.desc: Hail punched a hole in the awning over your door.
lines: A few regulars help you patch it up.

133.name: Keep the Fire Lit
133.desc: The old folks say that on a Blood Moon night, the stove must never go out.
lines: You sit up all night minding the stove.

134.name: Airing the Quilts
134.desc: The sun is out for once, and the whole street has hung their quilts out to air.
lines: Everyone with fresh, sunny bedding is in a great mood.

135.name: Water Off for Half a Day
135.desc: The town is repairing the water mains, so the water is off for half a day.
lines: The kitchen has to make do with buckets of stored water.

136.name: School Open Day
136.desc: It's open day at the primary school, and parents bring their kids in to eat.
lines: The place livens up in no time.

137.name: Battle of the Speakers
137.desc: Two dance groups in the square are trying to drown out each other's speakers.
lines: Once they've danced themselves out, they all come to rest their feet at your place.

138.name: The Parcel Point Moves In
138.desc: The parcel pickup point has moved in next door.
lines: People collecting parcels pop in for a bite on the way.

139.name: New Place Across the Street
139.desc: A new restaurant has opened across the street, and there's a long queue outside on opening day.
lines: Go and try it
You learn a thing or two.
Ignore it
Some customers wander over to join their queue.

140.name: The Wedding Party
140.desc: A couple about to marry want to book out your whole restaurant for their wedding reception.
lines: Accept
Walk-ins can't get in, but the couple pays generously.
Politely decline
You wish them a long and happy marriage.

141.name: A Regular's Birthday
141.desc: It's an old regular's birthday, so you bring him a slice of cake.
lines: The whole restaurant sings "Happy Birthday".

142.name: The Night Market Opens
142.desc: A night market has opened on the street outside your door.
lines: Wave after wave of tired shoppers drop in for a sit-down.

143.name: The Stallholders' Squabble
143.desc: Two stallholders at the Market are bickering, each shouting a lower price than the other.
lines: When they're done, they each toss a handful into your basket.

144.name: The Rider Race
144.desc: The riders have started racing each other to see who delivers fastest.
lines: It's faster, sure, but now and then a little soup gets spilled.

145.name: Takeaway Deals
145.desc: The takeaway app is running a "spend more, save more" promotion.
lines: Orders suddenly come pouring in.

146.name: The Hood Goes on Strike
146.desc: The range hood has broken down, and the kitchen is full of smoke.
lines: You have to cook slowly over a low flame with the windows open.

147.name: Leaky Roof
lines: You put a basin on Table 3.

148.name: The Daily's Reporter
148.desc: A reporter from the Town Daily comes to interview you: "What's the secret behind your house specialty?"
lines: Tell the truth: "I just cook with care."
When the piece comes out, customers find you refreshingly down-to-earth.
Talk it up: "A secret family recipe, three generations old!"
Crowds come in, with very high expectations.

149.name: The Lost Wallet
149.desc: You find a wallet under one of the tables.
lines: Hand it in to the police station
The owner gets it back and comes by specially to thank you.
Keep it at the front desk until someone claims it
The owner turns up in the afternoon and stays for a meal.

150.name: Rainbow After the Rain
150.desc: The rain has stopped, and a rainbow hangs in the sky.
lines: Customers all rush to the door for photos, then come back and order another dish.

151.name: A Review in the Paper
151.desc: The Town Daily ran an anonymous food review, and it's about your restaurant.
lines: "A quiet, honest little place."

152.name: The Show in the Square
152.desc: The young violinist is putting on a show in the square.
lines: After one song, he says: "This one's for the restaurant on the corner."

153.name: Marigolds and Sugar Skulls
153.desc: Every household sets orange marigolds and little sugar skulls by the door, and leaves a bowl of a departed loved one's favorite dish on the table.
lines: Lots of people come in and order "the one the old folks always used to get."

154.name: The Drum Parade
154.desc: A parade pounding big drums, all in sequins, passes down the street and dances until dawn.
lines: Worn-out dancers drop in for a late-night bite.

155.name: Swing Blindfolded
155.desc: The neighbors are throwing a kid's birthday party, with a paper candy pot hanging from a tree. The kids insist you put on a blindfold and take a swing.
lines: Swing hard
Way off. The kids are in stitches.
The pot cracks open, and out fall candy and a voucher.
Let the birthday kid have a go
The birthday kid nails it, and the whole family comes to your place for cake.

156.name: The Shared Gourd
156.desc: A table of customers sits in a circle, passing one gourd cup of bitter tea around and topping it up with hot water, pot after pot.
lines: They stay all afternoon, in great spirits.

157.name: Backyard Coals
157.desc: First thing this morning the neighbor lit a charcoal fire out back, and a huge cut of meat has been slow-roasting there all day.
lines: The smell drifts halfway down the street.

158.name: A Dance Under the Streetlamp
158.desc: Two old folks dance under the streetlamp outside your door. Step, pause, step: slow and steady.
lines: A crowd gathers to watch, and afterwards everyone comes in for a seat.

159.name: Grilled Corn from a Cart
159.desc: A cart parks at your door selling grilled corn slathered with cheese and chili powder.
lines: Corn in hand, people pop in for a bowl of soup on the way.

160.name: Three O'Clock Rain
160.desc: At three on the dot, a downpour arrives right on schedule, and ten minutes later it's over.
lines: People who ducked in out of the rain sit down and never leave.

161.name: The Bus Covered in Flowers
161.desc: An old bus painted all over with flowers and birds stops at the corner. Its horn plays a little song.
lines: Every passenger who gets off is drawn in by your sign.

162.name: The Customer Who Keeps His Mask On
162.desc: A muscular customer in a patterned mask sits down to order, and won't take the mask off even to eat.
lines: Ask for his autograph
He signs a napkin with a grand, swirling flourish.
Ask his real name
He finishes eating in silence and leaves you just one line: "The mask is my face."

163.name: Dance Tune on the Radio
163.desc: The kitchen radio starts playing a dance tune with a heavy beat, and everyone chopping and washing up starts swaying along.
lines: Hands move a lot faster, and the burners get turned up a notch.

164.name: Confetti Eggs
164.desc: A gang of kids with eggshells full of confetti is cracking them over everyone's head.
lines: Buy a few and fight back
You get the ringleader, and everyone bursts out laughing.
Hide in the restaurant
You still end up covered in confetti.

165.name: The Fifteenth Birthday
165.desc: A family wants to throw their daughter's fifteenth birthday party at your place, with dancing and a three-tier cake.
lines: Take the booking
Music and laughter all night, and a very pretty bill.
Politely decline
They go elsewhere, but leave you a slice of cake on the way out.

166.name: A Little Cup of Hot Chocolate
166.desc: An old lady ground cocoa on a stone mill, added cinnamon and a pinch of chili, and brings you a little cup.
lines: It warms you right through, and gives you ideas for the kitchen.

167.name: Street Kickabout
167.desc: Some kids are kicking a ball around out front, and one boots it straight into your restaurant.
lines: Give the ball back
The kids shout their thanks and run off.
Go out and play with them
You score a goal, and the kids mob you, cheering.
You take a tumble and rip a hole in your pants.

168.name: The Old Tree Bears Fruit
168.desc: The old tree out back has never borne a single fruit. Today it's suddenly loaded with avocados.
lines: Pick them for the kitchen
You fill a whole basket.
Share them with the neighbors
The neighbors all come by to say thanks, and stay for a meal.

169.name: Serenade Below the Window
169.desc: A band in wide-brimmed hats, with guitars and trumpets, sings a whole love song under the window across the street.
lines: The window never opens, so they console themselves with a meal at your place.

170.name: Little Monsters at the Door
170.desc: A bunch of kids dressed as little monsters knock on your door: "Trick or treat!"
lines: Hand out candy
The kids cheer and run off to the next house.
Pretend you're not home
The next day your front is draped in toilet paper, and you spend the morning cleaning up.

171.name: Pumpkins by the Door
171.desc: The neighbors line up pumpkins carved with spooky faces by their doors, and light candles in them after dark.
lines: People who come to see the pumpkins stay for dinner.

172.name: A Big Roast Turkey
172.desc: Today every family gathers around a big roast turkey, and afterwards everyone is too stuffed to move.
lines: Desserts sell like crazy tonight.

173.name: The Line Before Dawn
173.desc: Before sunrise, the whole town is lined up outside the mall for the big sales.
lines: The morning is dead quiet, then at noon all the bargain hunters pour in at once.

174.name: Free Refills
174.desc: A customer holds up an empty cup: "Refills are free, right?"
lines: Free
Now the whole street knows your refills are free.
Not free
The customer grumbles, but pays anyway.

175.name: The Insistent Tip
175.desc: After eating, a customer presses a roll of cash into the server's hand, saying that's just how it's done.
lines: The server is happy all day, and hands the roll in at the counter.

176.name: Late-Night Truckers
176.desc: A few long-haul truckers pull up at your door late at night, and each orders a big plate of fried eggs and a pot of coffee.
lines: Before leaving, they agree to stop by again next time they're passing.

177.name: Movies in the Parking Lot
177.desc: A big screen has gone up in the parking lot outside town, and everyone watches the film from their cars.
lines: Takeaway orders keep arriving at car windows, one after another.

178.name: Hot Dog Eating Contest
178.desc: Someone's holding an eating contest outside your door: whoever eats the most in ten minutes wins.
lines: Sign up
You put away twelve in one go and take the title!
You raise your hand and give up on the third one.
Be the judge
You count carefully, and nobody can fault you.

179.name: Red, White and Blue Fireworks
179.desc: Fireworks go off over town all night, filling the sky with red, white and blue.
lines: Everyone's hungry after the show.

180.name: Garage Sale Next Door
180.desc: The neighbors have set up in front of their garage selling old stuff, all of it for next to nothing.
lines: Go have a rummage
You find an old cookbook with notes scribbled all over the margins.
An old tin box has two vouchers hidden inside.
Skip it
You glance out the window and keep chopping.

181.name: The Big Game
181.desc: The whole town is watching a big game today, and everyone says the halftime ads are better than the game.
lines: Launch takeaway chicken wings
The wings go out box after box.
Put a big screen up in the restaurant
The place fills with customers in jerseys, and the cheering nearly lifts the roof.

182.name: The Groundhog and Its Shadow
182.desc: The townsfolk gather around a groundhog, waiting for it to poke its head out and look for its shadow, to tell how much winter is left. Will it see its shadow?
lines: It will
It sees its shadow. You guessed right! Six more weeks of winter.
It doesn't see its shadow. You guessed wrong.
It won't
It doesn't see its shadow. You guessed right! Spring is almost here.
It sees its shadow. You guessed wrong.

183.name: "That's It?"
183.desc: A customer looks down at the plate: "That's it?"
lines: Add a big extra scoop
He eats happily and tells everyone how generous your portions are.
Explain that it's fine dining
He's not quite convinced, but he licks the plate clean.

184.name: The Ice Cream Truck Tune
184.desc: An ice cream truck rolls slowly by, playing its tinkly tune, with kids chasing after it.
lines: Worn-out kids drag their parents in for a meal.

185.name: The Barbecue Contest Next Town Over
185.desc: The next town is holding a barbecue contest. The judges say all it takes to win is plenty of smoke and a sweet enough sauce.
lines: Enter
Your barbecue wins the blue ribbon!
The judges say your sauce is too fancy.
Go and watch
You stand in the smoke all afternoon and pick up a couple of tricks.

186.name: Cards in the Basement
186.desc: The radio says it'll be very windy today, so the neighbors all take shelter in your basement and play cards all afternoon.
lines: When the cards make them hungry, they order food.

187.name: The Welcome-Back Parade
187.desc: The town high school is welcoming its old students back, and the marching band, floats and cheerleaders parade right past your door.
lines: Students and parents pack the place.

188.name: Sunday Brunch
188.desc: A group of friends shows up at ten and orders a whole table of pancakes, eggs and juice.
lines: They chat into the afternoon and keep ordering more.

189.name: A Meal for the Next Customer
189.desc: At the counter, a customer pays for one extra meal, a treat for whoever walks in next.
lines: The next customer stands there stunned for a while, then pays for an extra meal too. People keep it going all day.

190.name: Episode One
190.desc: The whole town has started following a long-running TV drama. For the hour it's on, the streets are empty.
lines: Once it's over, everyone comes in to talk about the plot, and nobody fusses about the food.

191.name: The Twin Sister
191.desc: The heroine's long-lost twin sister has turned up on the show. Your customers are arguing over whether she's good or bad, and insist you pick a side.
lines: She's good
Her fans give you a round of applause.
She's bad
The other half give you a round of applause.

192.name: Amnesia
192.desc: The hero on the show took a fall and forgot everyone.
lines: Viewers all over town are dabbing their eyes in your restaurant, and everything tastes wonderful to them.

193.name: The Finale
193.desc: Tonight is the finale, and the twin sister's true identity is finally coming out.
lines: Show it in the restaurant
You called it! The whole place applauds you.
You called it wrong, and the customers tease you all night.
Skip it and focus on cooking
You only hear how it ended from customers the next day.

194.name: The Alpaca at the Door
194.desc: An alpaca followed some tourists into your restaurant, and now it's munching the potted plant by the door and won't leave.
lines: Call the owner
The owner soon comes to lead it away, apologizing over and over.
Feed it some greens and let it stay a while
Customers line up to take photos with it.

195.name: The Scarf in the Mail
195.desc: The alpaca's owner mailed you a scarf knitted from its wool.
lines: It's ridiculously soft, and you're in a great mood all day.

196.name: The Alpaca Is Back
196.desc: That alpaca found its own way back, and now stands at your door as straight as a doorman.
lines: Everyone walking by has to come in for a look.

197.name: The Ranch in the Hills
197.desc: The alpaca's owner invites you to visit the ranch up in the hills.
lines: Go
The owner gives you a basket of homemade cheese and mountain greens.
Another time
The owner mails you a photo of you and the alpaca.

198.name: Three Thousand Kilometers
198.desc: A camper van pulls up at your door. The family says they've driven three thousand kilometers already, with three thousand more to go.
lines: Give them a bag of snacks for the road
The kids wave to you from the windows.
Draw them a map of a shortcut
Dad folds up the map and tucks it into his shirt pocket.

199.name: Postcard from the Canyon
199.desc: They sent a postcard of a red canyon. On the back: "The snacks ran out ages ago. We miss your restaurant."
lines: You stick the postcard up by the counter, and every customer has to take a look.

200.name: Postcard from the Canyon
200.desc: They sent a postcard of a red canyon. On the back: "Your shortcut really was shorter. It saved us a whole day."
lines: Your riders used that map to work out a few more shortcuts of their own.

201.name: Passing Back Through
201.desc: That camper van is parked at your door again. The family is on the way home, with a box of local goodies picked up along the road.
lines: You all sit down together in the restaurant for a reunion dinner.

202.name: The Kid in the Corner
202.desc: A kid in glasses sits in the corner every day after school memorizing words. He says he's entering the town spelling contest.
lines: Quiz him
You test him on dish names from the menu, and he doesn't miss a single one.
Make him a bowl of noodles for luck
He eats until he's dripping with sweat, and swears he'll win.

203.name: Into the Final
203.desc: That kid runs in shouting: he made the final!
lines: Your customers all applaud him, and someone buys him a juice on the spot.

204.name: Final Night
204.desc: Tonight is the spelling final, and word is the last word will be the name of a dish.
lines: Go cheer him on
He spells the last word right and wins!
He's one letter off and takes second place.
Wait for news at the restaurant
He runs over to tell you he won!
He runs over to say he came second, and he's not the least bit upset.

205.name: Photo with the Trophy
205.desc: The kid brings you a photo: him holding the trophy, with your restaurant's front door behind him.
lines: You hang it in the most prominent spot on the wall.

206.name: The Wrap Truck
206.desc: A food truck selling wraps parks at your door, and the smell lures all your customers away.
lines: Go say hi and suggest teaming up
The owner is an easygoing guy, and you agree to talk more tomorrow.
Put up a "Today's Special" sign to compete
He puts up a sign too, and his prices beat yours.

207.name: The Combo Deal
207.desc: Your soup plus his wraps: together you launch a combo meal.
lines: They sell like crazy.

208.name: Price War
208.desc: The truck cut its prices again today, and the line outside it is longer than the one in your restaurant.
lines: Cut yours further
More customers, but less profit.
Invite the owner to dinner to make peace
You share a drink and agree to each stick to your own thing.

209.name: The Truck Moves On
209.desc: The truck is heading to the next town. Before leaving, the owner gives you a jar of his secret hot sauce.
lines: You add a spoonful to a dish, and customers keep asking what that flavor is.

210.name: The Man with His Hat Pulled Low
210.desc: A detective in a trench coat, hat brim pulled low, walks in and asks if you've seen anyone lately "carrying a red recipe book".
lines: Tell him honestly you haven't
He nods, leaves a business card, and goes.
Invite him to sit and tell you more
He drinks three coffees and tells a very long story.

211.name: The Torn-Out Page
211.desc: In the back alley you find a torn-out red page with half a recipe written on it.
lines: You try out the first half, and it's surprisingly good.

212.name: The Detective Returns
212.desc: The detective is back, and right away he spots the page you've tucked under the counter.
lines: Hand over the page
He says now he can close the case, and slips you two vouchers as thanks.
Refuse to give it up
He shrugs and leaves. You spend the evening studying half a recipe.

213.name: The Truth
213.desc: The Town Daily ran a short item: the owner of the red recipe book is a retired old chef who just forgot where he'd put it.
lines: The old chef comes all the way to your place for a meal, and says your cooking tastes like his did when he was young.

214.name: A Drum Band in the Backyard
214.desc: A drum band wants to borrow your backyard for practice. Just one afternoon, they say.
lines: Say yes
The drumming makes the pots jump, but the customers love it.
Say no
They go to the park, and you get a quiet afternoon.

215.name: Parade Night
215.desc: As the drum band's parade passes your door, they stop and play a piece just for you.
lines: The whole street gathers round to dance, then everyone piles into your restaurant.

216.name: The Signed Drumhead
216.desc: The drum band sends over an old drumhead covered in signatures, and you hang it on the wall.
lines: Two vouchers are taped to the back.

217.name: The Map on the Napkin
217.desc: A white-bearded old man says his grandpa buried a jar of gold in the hills out back, and the map is drawn on this napkin.
lines: Go digging with him
You dig up a rusty jar, and there really is something inside!
You dig all afternoon and only turn up an old spoon.
Treat him to a meal first
After eating, he leaves the napkin with you.

218.name: The Back of the Napkin
218.desc: You flip the napkin over: the back is crammed with a recipe for a stew.
lines: You cook up a pot, and the whole street can smell it.

219.name: The Old Man's Letter
219.desc: A letter arrives from the old man, far away: "The gold was a fib. The stew is the real thing."
lines: You laugh for ages, and everything goes right in the kitchen that day.
